solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hidden in bed?

blocks.note: first meaning: secret, operating in disguise
second meaning, read literally: tucked beneath the bedclothes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: someone in bed lies beneath the duvet.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents working in disguise are said to operate covertly, and someone tucked beneath blankets is literally that way.

clue.text: Scam set up with head of Ops? Impossible!

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards
the head of something is its top, here the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
and means together with
the opening letter of Ops

explanation.surface: A fraud is plotted with the operations chief, who flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase is a blunt refusal, telling someone that a request just cannot be done.

clue.text: Meteor seen only from time to time — that is weird

indicators.text: seen only from time to time
indicators.note: something seen only now and then shows up at intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Meteor
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A meteor that appears only now and then seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: That is gives IE, with the is absorbed into the abbreviation i.e.; is is then the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in an unsettling, spooky way, which is a close sense of uncanny.

clue.text: Law enforcement officer torn about a joint custodial role

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the combined pieces wrap around the last one

blocks.note: cop is informal for a police officer
rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer feels divided over sharing custody of a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The policeman and the word for torn sit together, then go around the a.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated parents who share responsibility for raising a child each act in this shared capacity.

clue.text: Frantically force one device to accept new online call

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one letter is taken into the group of words
doing something frantically means wildly and in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone desperately tries to make a gadget take an incoming internet call.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting held over the internet with participants seen on camera is a modern online call between several people.

clue.text: In the States, buildings made from concrete last indefinitely in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to where each word finishes, so only their closing letters are used

blocks.note: concrete means real, as opposed to abstract
the final letters of last and indefinitely

explanation.surface: American buildings made of concrete endure for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Concrete reads as the building material but means tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this word means real estate, the property of land together with the houses and structures on it.

clue.text: Intelligence obtained from wiretaps, retrospectively

indicators.note: something obtained from a word is taken out of it, so the letters sit inside the next word
looking back in time suggests reading the letters backwards, from the end to the start

blocks.note: a run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: Spies gather secrets after the fact by listening back to recorded phone taps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read wiretaps backwards, SPATERIW, and PATE sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pate is the head, and by extension the brains or wit inside it, as in an informal word for one's mental capacity.

clue.text: Every single elite runner initially following favourite coach

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of those words are taken

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
each means every single one
the opening letters of elite and runner

explanation.surface: Each top athlete trains under the same favoured coach.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, school sport; the favourite piece goes first because the others follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports instructor trains pupils in games and exercise, which is the job of a coach.

clue.text: Get loan arranged for hybrid

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are set out differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a loan to buy a hybrid car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit bred by crossing a tangerine with a pomelo or grapefruit, so it is a cross.

clue.text: Plant one found next to river

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A lone plant spotted growing on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so a garden maple is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Production of media content from case about a police operation

blocks.note: a pod is the case holding peas or seeds
CA is short for circa, Latin for about
a sting is an undercover operation to catch criminals

explanation.surface: A true-crime show built from a court case concerning a police operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Making and releasing downloadable audio series online is exactly the kind of media production the definition describes.

clue.text: Kitted out and ready to roll?

blocks.note: first meaning: wearing one's equipment or clothing
second meaning: a car with its transmission engaged, set to move off

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one prepared person; the two halves are separate senses, one about clothing and one about a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing your equipment means having your kit on, and a vehicle with the transmission engaged is set to move off.

clue.text: Dismissed tabloid editor is highly offended

blocks.note: a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out
rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A sacked red-top newspaper editor is furious about losing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To be incensed or indignant is to feel deeply insulted, which matches being very much offended.

clue.text: Sign of division can ultimately exhaust military unit

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a comma is a punctuation mark that divides a sentence
the final letter of can
do can mean tire out, as in done in

explanation.surface: A division sign at the end of a sum can wear out a student.
explanation.walkthrough: Sign of division looks like the maths symbol; here it is a punctuation mark that separates clauses.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are a specially trained force of soldiers, and the word also names the troop or raiding group itself.

clue.text: Guy that reinvented an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: to reinvent something is to remake it in a new form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: a guy is a man
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender who came up with a new cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a classic cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters, so it is a mixed spirit-based beverage.

clue.text: Bear circling around ring

indicators.note: to circle around is to turn back on oneself, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous storybook bear

explanation.surface: A circus bear walks round and round the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, such as one used in games or for a barrel, so it is a kind of round loop.

clue.text: American’s work protects awesome region of Canada

indicators.note: something that protects another surrounds and shields it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, work
rad is slang for excellent or cool

explanation.surface: American workers guard a magnificent stretch of Canadian wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland part of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador, a large northeastern area.

clue.text: Somewhat majestic, one-time revered figure

indicators.note: somewhat means only partly, so just a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: letters running across the end of majestic and the start of one

explanation.surface: A former celebrity once revered as rather regal.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a person widely admired and venerated as a symbol, such as a pop or fashion idol.

clue.text: Saloon possibly introducing remarkably meat-focused dining option?

blocks.note: a saloon is a type of car, a sedan in American English
very means extremely, remarkably

explanation.surface: A bar that unusually starts serving a meaty menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Saloon suggests a bar, which fits the dining picture; it is a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a British restaurant or buffet where roast joints of meat are sliced to order for diners.

clue.text: Outrageous tirade about the Union Jack?

blocks.note: the Union Jack is the national flag of the UK
a rant is a tirade about something

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a shocking diatribe about the British flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads naturally as a rant about a flag, so the two pieces are joined in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and shocking in its openness, so the word conveys something scandalous.

clue.text: Part of the service verbally criticise flyer

indicators.note: verbally means in speech, so the words count by how they are pronounced

blocks.note: to knock is to criticise
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: During a church service someone speaks out against a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the sections of the night office of matins in church liturgy, so a portion of worship.

clue.text: Inferior, dilapidated banger acquired by company

indicators.note: something acquired by another is taken into its possession, so it goes inside

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a banger is British slang for an old car, and a run-down one is a heap

explanation.surface: A firm buys a battered old car of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is slang for something low-priced and shoddy, so it means poor or second-rate.

clue.text: Extent of power held by a service provider?

indicators.note: something held by another thing is gripped within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: per means a, as in five pounds a day
reach is the range or extent of one's influence

explanation.surface: How far a utility company's power supply stretches across the region.
explanation.walkthrough: Service provider suggests a utility or broadband firm; the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman leading worship delivers sermons, so a church minister literally provides the Sunday service.

clue.text: Censor radical piece of legislation

blocks.note: red is a common label for a political radical
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wants to ban an extreme new law.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to black out or remove sensitive text before release, which is a form of censoring.

clue.text: Took out old hat

blocks.note: first meaning: went out romantically with someone
second meaning: old-fashioned, behind the times

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like removing an old piece of headgear; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting someone means going on romantic outings with them, and anything unfashionable or behind the times is passé.

clue.text: Take it easy, then come down extremely even-tempered and calm

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters at each end of the word

blocks.note: to rest is to relax
rain is what comes down from the sky
the first and last letters of even-tempered

explanation.surface: Advice to relax and then settle down, staying composed and serene.
explanation.walkthrough: Even-tempered looks like part of the definition, but only its outer letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restrained keeps emotions under control, showing a composed and measured manner, which is being unruffled.

clue.text: Person likely to acquire the first tranche of tickets released?

definitions.text: Person likely to acquire the first tranche of tickets released?

indicators.note: the first tranche is the opening batch, so just the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of tickets
something released has been let out

explanation.surface: A scalper snaps up the first batch of tickets as soon as they go on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket tout buys up seats for popular events as soon as sales open, then resells them at inflated prices.

clue.text: That’s the chap yelling out Abide With Me, maybe

indicators.note: yelling out means saying something loudly, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

blocks.note: pointing at a man and saying that's the one

explanation.surface: Someone points out the man belting out a famous hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: Abide With Me is a hymn traditionally sung at the English FA Cup Final.
explanation.definitionFit: Abide With Me is a well-known Christian song of praise, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Major sick of being in a cavalry?

blocks.note: to be over something is to be tired of it
cavalry soldiers spend their service on horseback

explanation.surface: An army major fed up with serving in a mounted regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Major looks like the army rank, which fits the cavalry picture; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is the most important one, taking precedence over everything else, so it is paramount.
